AVOID!!!
Sep 2012 • Couples
I have been living in HCMC for several years and know this restaurant for quite some time.

After my visit it is clear that this restaurant lives off his former reputation:

We ordered four dishes- one was ok, two of them uneatable and last dish, the tuna in a clay pot, was too salty. We informed the waitress about the salty tuna and asked her to bring us a new, less salty dish. 
She takes the dish, tests it and brings it back to the kitchen.

After a few minutes she appears again and brings us the same dish she tested, just re-cooked in water. 
We refused to eat it and returned it. Fed up we the restaurant, we asked for the bill and to our surprise they charged the tuna! We argued with them to no avail. We had to pay 90.000D for a dish you get in a street restaurant for 15.000D. 

This was by far my worst experience in 5 years HCMC.

Good Vietnamese food designed for locals rather than tourists
Nov 2011
Upfront I have to say I was a little surprised by the recent review navalator. I have been to Green Rice many times over the past 2-3 years, given my frequent visits to Vietnam on business. I often wonder what people have as expectations when visiting hotels, restaurants, etc. The restaurant in the Park Hyatt has expectations (and pretensions) to high quality food, prices and service, mainly for foreigners and the wealthy locals. Then there are the mid range restaurants suitable for the mid range tourists, Green Rice is not one of them. It is not low range but it is for the locals and their families, with prices to boot AND it is relatively inexpensive. What I will agree on is the ordinary level of service and lack of English - something I have mentioned to them but as I usually go with locals, less of an issue for me and I can get by with Pho Ga/Bo! Anyway back to my review:

Always for breakfast! The traditional Vietnamese pancakes are made fresh and you can watch them being made - always nice for kids. My fave is the pho. Nothign like that to start the day, mind you I can eat it for lunch and dinner too. Try getting the coffee right, hmm.

I love the Hmong Black Chicken possibly a bit better than another reviewer but I think that is due to not knowing what the dish is and what the Vietnamese like for this dish. It is not a western (lots of plumb chicken dish) meal. Too me, cannot get enough of the fish dishes - choose a fresh one straight from the tank. Eels are sometimes pointing at the other tank and saying, choose them, choose them, those carp are yummy!

At night under the most enormous Banyon Tree with fairy lights is quite magic. Sit back, have a few drinks and enjoy the meal. If you don't like the heat so much, they have a few AC dining rooms as well.

It seats about 300 people I guess so keep that in mind when visiting, it is not one of those little local places.

Pluses: good local food and prices and amazing outdoor terrace.
Minus: lack of english staff but most of the menu has translations and sometimes they can be a bit slow.
Suggestion: Chill out but if not gettign service, call over a staff member and ask for the english speaker if getting no where, there just might be one in the kitchen or bar!

Deceptive Trap
Oct 2011
This shop is located at the end of something that looks like a broad alley. It is very attractive with hundreds of fairy lights hanging from the many trees in the courtyard. Upon approaching the entrance we were met by a manager who seemed comatose. In Vietnamese we asked for a table for two. We waited about 5 minutes for him to return and escort us to a table. There were about one hundred tables available and all empty. We wondered why he had to take that amount of time to find an available table. We then sat for another 10 minutes waiting for a menu. When we reviewed the menu prices we found them astronomical. We ordered appetizers and mains and it was another 40 minutes before the appetizers arrived cold. They were essentially inedible. The service was markedly disdainful and unconcerned. We decided that we had had enough and tried vainly to obtain the notice of a waiter. When a busser walked by we collared him to tell our waiter to bring the check. A female cashier brought the check which, to our consternation and disgust, contained charges for napkins and un-ordered water. We refused to pay for the napkin and phantom water and walked out. I would not recommend this place to a starving shipwrecked sailor. Caution: Do not be hoodwinked by the fairy lights!

Chic Ethnic Cuisine
Oct 2011
Ethnic cuisine is probably not a politically correct descriptor, but the food and environment isn't quite Western. 

Location/Getting There: Turn into a side street from a busy one, pass several apartment blocks, hundreds of parked motorbikes and a cinema to the end of a cul-de-sac and arrive at a large courtyard with simulated green wicker chairs and tables under the cover of umbrellas and trees ornamented with fairy lights.

Atmosphere/Decor: Patrons not interested in eating outdoors in the courtyard can sit in the verandah underneath the European style building overlooking the courtyard or sit in an air-conditioned indoor dining room looking into the street (with parked motorbikes).

Service: Since my partner and I were the only patrons at the restaurant, we basically had each a private waiter for either of us (early in the evening on a Monday). The waiters were not overly attentive/hovering but were prompt when waved to come over to our table. We tried to ask for green rice (the restaurant's namesake) and were served white rice instead. I still haven't figured out if this was due to the staff's limited English or they really. didn't have green rice. Table service included one spoon and a pair of chopsticks. Since there were no napkins (paper or linen), we were offered two limp, thin, damp towelettes (and later to find from the bill that each towelette cost 2,000VND ~ 0.10 USD)

Food, Cost and Quality: I ordered an avocado milk shake, which was absolutely scrumptious (90,000VND ~ 4.5USD). For entree, I ordered baked H'mong chicken. It arrived (at the same time as my partner's food) in very large crock pot (very impressive). However, as I picked through the contents of the crock pot, I realize that the contents were half herbs while the other half black chicken skin, bones and very little meat (295,000VND ~ 14.5USD). The little meat that I was able to consume was not overly pungent but extremely fragrant. It reminded me of medicine from a Chinese apothecary. 

Conclusion: I probably won't go back to the restaurant or recommend my friends to go there for a meal (I might consider going back for the avocado shake). The atmosphere is very chic, but I felt I didn't get much bang for my dong!

'Com Xanh - Green Rice Restaurant, a real gem in central Saigon!
I discovered a great restaurant on my recent trip to Ho Chi Minh city. It's called Com Xanh - Green Rice Restaurant and is located in District 1, in the central / downtown area. 

I went thefore for breakfast one day, and love it so much that I ended up going back there at different points to try their lunch and dinner! 

For breakfast I tried the delicious freshly made rice pancakes... the lady who makes them is known by the staff as the 'Pancake Queen'!! she sits on her stool and makes pancake after delicous pancake!! Also can recommend their fresh fruit juices... strawberry was my favourite. 

Lunch time is great, as the large terrace where most of of the tables are is shadowed by a large 100 year old tree, which keeps you cool. 

Then at dinner the place has a wondeful atmosphere... strings of fairy lights hang from the large tree, with the terraced area being atmoshperically lit. The sound of the manmade waterfall and the live music that they seem to have their every evening make the ambience enchanting! In terms of food, my favourite had to be the spring rolls... but there were so many lovely things to chose from. I was also happy / and amazed to see that they have one of my favourite French wines on their wine list... the red Pinot Noir by 'Bouchard Pere & Fils'!

Whether for breakfast, lunch or dinner I can highly recommend this restaurant.. very friendly, efficient service, great food and atmosphere! I think I would definitely have a preference for dinner tho due to the lovely atmosphere!

Here is the address: 

Com Xanh - Green Rice Restaurant
6 Thai Van Lung St
District 1, Ho Chi Minh City 

(not far from theatre, Park Hyatt Hotel, Continental Hotel, Caravelle hotel etc)
